extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and institutional compliance/legal officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for institutions to prevent, investigate, and resolve sex discrimination and sex-based harassment under Title IX, including duties of the Title IX Coordinator, notification and confidentiality rules, supportive measures, investigation and adjudication standards, informal resolution, and appeal/dismissal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for employees
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary school or secondary school recipient must require all of its employees who are not confidential employees to notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part. All other recipients must, at a minimum, require: (i) any non-confidential employee who has authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information; and (ii) all other non-confidential employees either (A) notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information, or (B) provide the coordinator's contact information and complaint process information to anyone who provides the employee with such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postsecondary institutions must reasonably determine whether a person who is both student and employee is subject to these requirements. The notification requirements do not apply to an employee who has personally been subject to the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify participants how to contact its confidential employees (if any). A confidential employee must explain to any person who informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination: (i) the employee's confidential status and the circumstances in which they are not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator; (ii) how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and make a complaint; and (iii) that the Title IX Coordinator may offer/support supportive measures and initiate informal resolution or an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude employees whose confidential status applies only to IRB-approved human-subjects research gathering information about sex discrimination from the requirement to publicize confidential employee contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of disclosures at public awareness events
rubrics_metrics.description: When a postsecondary institution's Title IX Coordinator is notified of information provided during a public awareness event held on campus or via an institution-sponsored online platform, the institution is not obligated to act in response to that information unless it indicates an imminent and serious threat to health or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not required to act, institutions must use information from such events to inform prevention efforts (e.g., tailored training for a particular program or location). There is no obligation for Title IX Coordinators or employees to attend public awareness events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duties upon notice
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the Title IX Coordinator must take actions to promptly and effectively end any sex discrimination, prevent recurrence, and remedy its effects, including: (i) treat complainant and respondent equitably; (ii) offer and coordinate supportive measures for complainant and, if procedures initiated, for respondent; (iii) notify complainant (or reporter if complainant unknown) and notify respondent, if complaint made, of grievance procedures and informal resolution options; (iv) in response to a complaint, initiate grievance procedures or informal resolution if appropriate and requested by all parties; (v) in absence of a complaint or after withdrawal, determine whether to initiate a complaint under the grievance procedures after considering specific factors; (vi) if initiating a complaint, notify the complainant prior to doing so and address reasonable safety concerns; and (vii) regardless of complaint initiation, take other appropriate prompt and effective steps to ensure sex discrimination does not continue or recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinator's determination in (v) must consider at minimum: the complainant's request not to proceed; complainant's reasonable safety concerns; risk of additional acts; severity of alleged discrimination (including whether removal or sanction would be necessary); age and relationship of parties (including if respondent is an employee); scope suggesting pattern or multiple victims; availability of evidence; and whether the recipient could end discrimination without initiating grievance procedures. If conduct presents an imminent and serious threat or prevents equal access, the Coordinator may initiate a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator discretion to decline action when conduct cannot constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator is not required to comply with the duties listed when, upon reasonable determination, the conduct as alleged could not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a gatekeeping discretion to avoid unnecessary procedures when allegations fail to meet Title IX coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: offering, design, and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer and coordinate supportive measures, as appropriate. Supportive measures may include counseling; extensions of deadlines and course adjustments; campus escorts; increased security; restrictions on contact; leaves of absence; changes in class, work, housing, extracurricular activities; and training/education programs related to sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden either party, must be designed to protect safety or restore access, and must not be imposed for punitive reasons. They may be modified or terminated at conclusion of grievance or informal resolution, or continued beyond. Parties must have a timely opportunity to seek modification/reversal from an appropriate impartial employee (not the original decisionmaker) who has authority to change the decision. Recipients must not disclose information about supportive measures to persons other than the person to whom they apply, unless necessary to provide the measure or when permitted by specified exceptions. Special consultation requirements apply for elementary/secondary students with disabilities (consult IEP team or placement decision group) and postsecondary students with disabilities (may consult designated disability support office) to ensure compliance with IDEA and Section 504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may remove a respondent from its education program or activity on an emergency basis provided it undertakes an individualized safety and risk analysis, determines an imminent and serious threat to health or safety justifies removal, and provides the respondent notice and an opportunity to challenge the decision immediately following removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision does not modify rights under IDEA, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, or the ADA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative leave
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may place an employee respondent on administrative leave from employment responsibilities during the pendency of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not modify rights under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act or the ADA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited disclosures of personally identifiable information
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not disclose personally identifiable information obtained in complying with this part, except in limited circumstances: (1) prior written consent from person with legal right to consent; (2) disclosure to parent/guardian/authorized legal representative with right to receive disclosures; (3) to carry out the purposes of this part (including actions to address conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination); (4) as required by Federal law, regulations, or terms of a Federal award; or (5) when required by State or local law or permitted under FERPA and not otherwise in conflict with Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides privacy protections while enumerating lawful or necessary disclosure exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to offer informal resolution prior to determination
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time prior to determining whether sex discrimination occurred, a recipient may offer complainant and respondent an informal resolution process, unless the complaint includes allegations that an employee engaged in sex-based harassment of an elementary or secondary student or such a process would conflict with law. The recipient may decline to offer informal resolution even if parties wish it, and may decline when alleged conduct presents future risk of harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient must not require or pressure parties to participate; must obtain voluntary consent and must not require waiver of the right to investigation/determination as a condition of enrollment or employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-initiation notice and content for informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiation of an informal resolution process, the recipient must provide notice that explains: (i) the allegations; (ii) the requirements of the informal resolution process; (iii) that any party may withdraw from informal resolution and initiate/resume grievance procedures; (iv) that agreement to a resolution precludes initiation/resumption of grievance procedures on same allegations; (v) potential terms that may be requested/offered (and that an informal resolution agreement is binding only on the parties); and (vi) what information the recipient will maintain and whether/how it could be disclosed for use in grievance procedures if initiated or resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The facilitator must not be the same person as the investigator or decisionmaker, must not have conflict of interest or bias, and must receive training under §106.8(d)(3). Potential informal resolution terms may include restrictions on contact and restrictions on participation or attendance equivalent to remedies or disciplinary sanctions that could be imposed through grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures: general written requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures for the prompt and equitable resolution of complaints of sex discrimination must be in writing and include provisions that incorporate the requirements of §106.45. Requirements related to a respondent apply only to sex discrimination complaints alleging a person violated the prohibition on sex discrimination; when a complaint alleges a recipient policy or practice discriminates on basis of sex, the recipient is not considered a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that procedures must be formalized in writing and aligned with the regulatory subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The following persons have a right to make a complaint requesting investigation and determination: (i) a complainant; (ii) a parent/guardian/other authorized legal representative with right to act on behalf of complainant; (iii) the Title IX Coordinator after making the determination specified in §106.44(f)(1)(v); and (iv) with respect to complaints other than sex-based harassment, any student or employee or any non-student/non-employee who was participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity at the time of the alleged discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who has standing to trigger the grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic requirements for grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures must: (1) treat complainants and respondents equitably; (2) require that persons designated as Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker not have conflicts of interest or bias (the decisionmaker may be same person as Coordinator or investigator); (3) include presumption that respondent is not responsible until determination; (4) establish reasonably prompt timeframes for major stages (with a process for reasonable extensions for good cause and notice of reason); (5) require reasonable steps to protect privacy without restricting parties' ability to obtain/present evidence or consult advisors; (6) require objective evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, with credibility determinations not based on status as complainant/respondent/witness; (7) exclude certain types of evidence/questions as impermissible; and (8) articulate consistent principles if adopting different procedures for different complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule specifies that major stages include evaluation (decision whether to dismiss or investigate), investigation, determination, and appeal. Paragraph (b)(7) lists impermissible evidence: (i) evidence protected by privilege or provided to a confidential employee unless waived; (ii) party/witness treatment records by medical/psychological professionals unless voluntary written consent; (iii) evidence relating to complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct unless offered to prove alternate perpetrator or prior sexual conduct with respondent to prove consent. Prior consensual sexual conduct alone does not demonstrate consent to alleged harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allegations content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon initiation of grievance procedures, a recipient must provide notice of the allegations to known parties. The notice must include: (i) the recipient's grievance procedures (and §106.46 if applicable) and any informal resolution process; (ii) sufficient information to allow parties to respond (identities of parties, conduct alleged, dates/locations as available); (iii) a statement that retaliation is prohibited; and (iv) a statement that parties are entitled to equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an accurate description of such evidence and, if description provided, access to evidence upon request. If additional allegations are later investigated, recipient must provide notice of those additional allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient information is defined to include identities, conduct, dates, and locations to the extent available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of a complaint — grounds and required procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a complaint for: (i) inability to identify respondent after reasonable steps; (ii) respondent not participating in recipient's education program/activity and not employed by recipient; (iii) complainant voluntarily withdraws allegations and, with Title IX Coordinator decline to initiate, remaining allegations would not constitute sex discrimination if proven; or (iv) recipient determines alleged conduct, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination. Prior to dismissal, recipient must make reasonable efforts to clarify allegations with complainant. Upon dismissal, recipient must promptly notify complainant (and respondent if already notified) of basis for dismissal. Recipient must notify complainant that dismissal may be appealed and provide opportunity to appeal on bases in §106.46(i)(1). If dismissal appealed, recipient must follow specified appeal procedures (notify parties of appeal, implement appeals equally, ensure appeal decisionmaker did not participate in investigation/dismissal, ensure appeal decisionmaker trained, provide parties equal opportunity to make statement, notify parties of result and rationale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dismissal occurs where respondent had been notified, the respondent must also be informed and offered supportive measures if appropriate. After dismissal, recipient must offer supportive measures and require Title IX Coordinator to take steps to ensure discrimination does not continue or recur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may consolidate complaints against more than one respondent, by more than one complainant against one or more respondents, or by one party against another party, when allegations arise out of the same facts or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one consolidated complaint involves sex-based harassment with a student complainant or respondent at a postsecondary institution, the grievance procedures must comply with §106.46 in addition to §106.45. When multiple parties are involved, references to party/complainant/respondent include plural as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint investigation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide for adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation. The recipient bears the burden to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence to determine whether sex discrimination occurred; must provide equal opportunity for parties to present fact witnesses and inculpatory/exculpatory evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible; must review all evidence and determine relevance and impermissibility; and must provide each party equal opportunity to access relevant evidence or an accurate description of it, with reasonable opportunity to respond and with reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosure of evidence obtained solely through grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures of such information are authorized for administrative proceedings or litigation related to the complaint. Review of evidence must be consistent with definition of relevant and impermissible evidence under §106.2 and paragraph (b)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning parties and witnesses to assess credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide a process that enables the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses to adequately assess credibility to the extent credibility is both in dispute and relevant to evaluating allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process should allow the decisionmaker to probe credibility when it matters to the outcome; specifics of questioning procedures are governed by the grievance framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination whether sex discrimination occurred
rubrics_metrics.description: Following investigation and evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, the recipient must: (1) use the preponderance of the evidence standard to determine whether sex discrimination occurred unless the recipient uses clear and convincing evidence in all other comparable proceedings and elects that standard; (2) notify parties in writing of the determination and rationale and appeal procedures; (3) if determination that sex discrimination occurred, require Title IX Coordinator to coordinate remedies to complainant and others affected, coordinate imposition of disciplinary sanctions on respondent (including notifying complainant of any sanctions), and take other steps to prevent recurrence; (4) comply with §106.45 and §106.46 before imposing disciplinary sanctions; and (5) not discipline participants for making a false statement or for engaging in consensual sexual conduct based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both standards of proof require decisionmaker to evaluate evidence for persuasiveness; determination must be based on persuasiveness, not quantity alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer parties an appeal process that, at minimum, is the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings, including other discrimination complaints. For complaints of sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or respondent, a postsecondary institution must also offer an appeal on the bases set out in §106.46(i)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal procedures must be implemented equally for parties and follow training/conflict-of-interest rules for appeal decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional provisions must apply equally
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts additional provisions as part of its grievance procedures for handling complaints (including sex-based harassment), such additional provisions must apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents ad hoc or one-sided procedural rules that advantage one party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution election in lieu of grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of resolving a complaint through the recipient's grievance procedures, the parties may elect to participate in an informal resolution process under §106.44(k) if provided by the recipient consistent with that paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cross-references the limitations and notice requirements for informal resolution described in §106.44(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions limited to sex-based harassment complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: For complaints alleging sex-based harassment, grievance procedures must: (1) describe the range of supportive measures available to complainants and respondents under §106.44(g); and (2) list or describe the possible disciplinary sanctions the recipient may impose and remedies it may provide following a determination that sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires transparency about potential remedies and sanctions specific to sex-based harassment findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures for sex-based harassment involving student complainants/respondents at postsecondary institutions (§106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution's written grievance procedures for prompt and equitable resolution of complaints of sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or student respondent must include provisions that incorporate the requirements of §106.45 and §106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a complainant or respondent is both a student and an employee, the institution must make a fact-specific inquiry to determine whether the requirements of §106.46 apply.
